Synopsis:
Research by Ordnance Survey, the Met Office, and 4 Earth Intelligence introduces a Heat Vulnerability Index for 71 royal charter cities across Great Britain. Portsmouth tops the ranking today and is projected to remain most exposed through 2100. By 2040, all 71 cities will reach high vulnerability; by 2100, nearly two-thirds could hit the most severe tier. Vulnerability is driven by hard surfaces, low green cover, and limited water features that trap heat — urban heat islands can run up to 10°C above surrounding rural areas. Leicester, Exeter, Nottingham, Bristol and Brighton are projected to climb sharply in rankings. Milton Keynes is the best-performing city due to extensive natural surfaces. The 2022 London heatwaves already cost an estimated £1.5bn in economic damage.
